sovereign_country.strategic_role: 北美成熟市场、联邦与省两级公司实体设立（EPC合规）

business_scope.primary_industry_name: Retail Sale via Internet - Marketplace FBA Store

meta_jurisdiction_context.legal_system_doctrine: Hybrid: Civil Law (Quebec private law under the Civil Code of Quebec), Common Law federal/administrative law, and statutory AML/CFT regime applying throughout Canada
applicable_bilateral_investment_treaties: Canada-EU Comprehensive Economic and Trade Agreement (CETA)
Canada-China Foreign Investment Promotion and Protection Agreement (FIPA)

ubo_and_aml_profiling.statutory_law_governance: Federal: Proceeds of Crime (Money Laundering) and Terrorist Financing Act, SC 2000, c 17; Criminal Code, RSC 1985, c C-46, ss 354, 462.31; Special Economic Measures Act, SC 1992, c 17; Canada Business Corporations Act, RSC 1985, c C-44, ss 140.8-140.803 (individuals with significant control). Quebec: Act respecting the legal publicity of enterprises, CQLR c P-45, arts 22, 23.1, 35.6-35.7, 38; Regulation respecting the application of the Act respecting the legal publicity of enterprises, CQLR c P-45, r 1; Civil Code of Quebec, arts 2186, 2236-2244; Quebec anti-money-laundering by-law under the Act respecting the legal publicity of enterprises.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certified copy of the Limited Partnership Agreement (Société en commandite) or equivalent foreign partnership constitutive deed
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Notary in the partner's country of origin and, where applicable, the competent companies registry of that country
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille or consular legalization if the source country is not a party to the Hague Convention

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of Good Standing / Certificate of Registered Address for each corporate general partner or corporate limited partner
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Competent corporate registry of the partner's jurisdiction of incorporation
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille or consular legalization before submission to the Registraire des entreprises du Québec

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Notarized passport copies, proof of residential address, and evidence of full legal name for each individual general partner, limited partner, and each beneficial owner crossing the 25% threshold
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Qualified notary or competent passport office in the country of residence
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille or equivalent consular legalization

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Bank reference letter confirming legitimate source of funds and no adverse AML history for the capital contribution
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Qualifying financial institution where initial LP contributions are held
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille or consular legalization, plus notarized signature/signature guarantee of the bank officer

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Civil Code of Québec, CQLR c CCQ-1991, arts. 2236–2250 (limited partnership); Act respecting the legal publicity of sole proprietorships, partnerships and legal persons, CQLR c P-45, ss. 1, 7, 15–39 (registration and publicity).
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Registraire des entreprises du Québec (Quebec Enterprise Registrar) — Espace entreprises online portal.
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Déclaration d'immatriculation — Société en commandite / Declaration of Registration of a Limited Partnership.
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No statutory minimum paid-up capital and no escrow requirement for a Québec limited partnership. Contributions are fixed in the partnership agreement and may be payable on call.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: BE IT RESOLVED, as general partner of [NAME] L.P., that the organization of the Partnership under Civil Code of Québec arts. 2236–2250 is approved; the partnership agreement and capital contribution schedule, including subscription by each partner in agreed amounts, are accepted; the registered office is established at [ADDRESS], Province of Québec; [Name] is appointed chairman-representative and [Name] is appointed secretary-treasurer for formation filings; each officer is authorized to execute and file the Declaration of Registration with the Registraire des entreprises du Québec, open the partnership bank account, and attend to all incidental formation formalities. All acts consistent with these resolutions are ratified.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Registraire des entreprises du Québec — online name reservation service
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Log in to the Registraire's Espace entreprises portal, perform a name search, submit a reserved-name application using the proposed French or bilingual name, and obtain the name reservation certificate valid for 90 days.
required_dossiers: Proof of identity of the filer
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the name is refused, file a revised name application with a new distinctive component or add a statutory declaration explaining the chosen name; the reservation is refiled without affecting other formation steps.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Private legal drafting; not filed with the Registraire
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Draft and execute a limited partnership agreement in writing, identifying the general partner, limited partners, contribution obligations, profit allocation, registered office, management powers, withdrawal rights, and dissolution events. All general and limited partners must execute the agreement or their attorneys-in-fact.
required_dossiers: Schedule of capital contributions and subscriptions
Power of attorney or signing authority for corporate partners
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Correct defective signature blocks, have the partners re-execute or ratify, and if an attorney-in-fact signs, attach a notarized power of attorney.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Subscription of Capital and Opening of Partnership Bank Account
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Canadian chartered bank or Québec credit union
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Open a partnership bank account in the exact registered legal name, deposit the agreed initial capital contributions, complete KYC/AML forms for all partners and beneficial owners, and maintain the required schedule of contributions.
required_dossiers: Certified copy of the limited partnership agreement
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the bank queries the application, provide updated source-of-funds evidence, amended beneficial ownership declarations, or choose another financial institution accepting non-resident limited partners.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Filing of Declaration of Registration with the Registraire des entreprises
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Registraire des entreprises du Québec — Espace entreprises electronic filing
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Complete the online declaration for a société en commandite, enter the exact legal name, registered office address, general partner identity and powers, aggregate capital contributed by limited partners, and principal establishment; attest, submit, and pay the filing fee; download the NEQ certificate.
required_dossiers: Identification of general and limited partners
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the Registraire issues a query, respond within 15 days; file a corrective declaration, amend partner information, or supplement the registered office documentation; the original registration remains valid while corrected.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Federal Business Number and Tax Program Accounts
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Canada Revenue Agency — Business Registration Online
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Use the CRA Business Registration Online service to register the partnership for a federal Business Number and the relevant program accounts: GST/HST, payroll, and import/export if directly purchasing or shipping inventory; connect the NEQ to the CRA BN.
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If program account registration is incorrect, call the CRA Business Window, request consolidation or amendment, and file an RC159 amendment where necessary.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Local municipality where the registered office or physical establishment is located
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Confirm the zoned use of the registered office or any physical establishment; obtain a municipal establishment permit only if a physical office or warehouse is occupied. For a pure virtual registered office serving an FBA seller, no municipal establishment permit is required.
required_dossiers: Lease or virtual office service agreement
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If zoning does not permit the office, apply for a minor variance or relocate the registered office to a compliant address; the municipal clerk may issue a certificate of authorization.

step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: After registration, maintain the statutory register and file an annual declaration with the Registraire; update any changes in general partner, limited partners, registered office, or establishment; pay the applicable annual fee.
required_dossiers: Changes to registered office or general partners
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the annual declaration is late, file an off-cycle declaration with the late fee; the Registraire may strike the enterprise if the debt remains unpaid; apply for reinstatement under the Legal Publicity Act.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Not applicable. No provincial industrial board licence is triggered for ISIC 4791 electronic marketplace retail; industrial permits are generally administered by the Ministère de l'Économie, de l'Innovation et de l'Énergie du Québec.
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Not applicable — Amazon FBA marketplace sellers under ISIC 4791 do not require a Québec industrial or manufacturing operating permit.

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Ministère de l'Environnement, de la Lutte contre les changements climatiques, de la Faune et des Parcs du Québec (MELCCFP)
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Exempt from mandatory environmental impact assessment under the Environment Quality Act, CQLR c Q-2, for online retail selling without industrial production, waste disposal, or listed contaminating infrastructure.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: No industrial discharge or VOC emission thresholds apply to an FBA seller. If an administrative office or small warehouse is occupied, wastewater discharges must meet municipal sewer by-laws and the Environmental Quality Act s. 20 water protection standard; air emissions remain subject to s. 197 only if equipment emits contaminants.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Fire safety certification is required under the Québec Building Code and local fire department by-laws before occupying any physical office or warehouse; structural load verification is required if racked storage is installed; workplace health and safety registration with CNESST is required only if employees are hired in Québec.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Canada Revenue Agency (CRA) / Agence du revenu du Canada (ARC), portal: www.canada.ca/taxes (My Business Account and Business Registration Online); and Revenu Québec (RQ), portal: www.revenuquebec.ca (Mon dossier d'entreprise). For a Quebec limited partnership, GST/HST (federal) is administered by CRA, while QST (Quebec Sales Tax) is administered by RQ under a parallel Quebec registration regime.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: (1) Assess non-resident supplier status for GST/HST and QST under the 2021 e-commerce deemed-supply rules; (2) obtain a federal Business Number (BN) for the LP by filing Form RC1 or using Business Registration Online (BRO), selecting the non-resident business program account for GST/HST (BN with 'RM' program account suffix); (3) register the LP with Revenu Québec for QST by submitting the Quebec registration application (electronically via Mon dossier d'entreprise or paper form combined with the RC1), obtaining a provincial QST number linked to the BN; (4) file the partnership information return T5013 (or T5013F for non-calendar fiscal periods) to report Canadian-source income and allocation to non-resident partners; (5) ensure each partner obtains a Canadian tax identifier and, where applicable, file NR6/T1/T2 or corporate returns; (6) where Amazon operates as a registered distribution platform operator collecting GST/QST on facilitated marketplace sales, the LP may not require its own GST/QST accounts for those sales alone, but registration becomes mandatory when the LP makes direct (non-platform) taxable sales from Canadian FBA inventory once worldwide taxable supplies exceed CAD 30,000; (7) appoint a Canadian representative/authorized agent where the LP has no Canadian establishment.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.default_entity_tax_classification: Pass_Through_Eligible; the LP is fiscally transparent for income tax purposes (Income Tax Act s. 96, with income computed at partnership level and allocated to partners), but is a separate 'person' and a distinct registrant for GST/HST/QST purposes; non-resident partners are taxable under ITA s. 2(3) on Canadian-source business income, subject to treaty protection and Part XIII withholding where applicable.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: Canada has no US-style check-the-box classification election. Available elections and integrity mechanisms: (i) non-calendar fiscal-period election for the partnership (ITA s. 249.1) with T5013F filing; (ii) ITA s. 216 election for non-resident partners with Canadian rental income; (iii) GST/HST annual, quarterly or monthly reporting-period election; (iv) combined GST/QST filing election with CRA/RQ reconciliation; (v) hybrid-mismatch integrity rules (ITA s. 18.2, 18.3, 247.12 and Part 12.6) effective for recent taxation years, with documentation elections to establish the taxable status of foreign entities and prevent double non-taxation; (vi) tax-treaty based elections and waiver filings for non-resident partners relying on Canada-US or other applicable income tax conventions.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: Federal GST (Goods and Services Tax) at 5% administered by CRA, plus provincial QST (Quebec Sales Tax) at 9.975% administered by Revenu Québec; Quebec is not an HST province and QST is computed on the selling price excluding GST; the combined effective indirect tax rate for taxable B2C supplies in Quebec is 14.975%.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: CAD 30,000 worldwide taxable supplies (GST/HST small-supplier threshold under ETA s. 148) and the parallel QST threshold; no threshold applies to marketplace platform operators that must collect GST/QST on facilitated sales of goods located in Canada (Amazon registers and remits regardless of volume); the foreign LP must register when its worldwide taxable supplies exceed CAD 30,000, and must also register for direct off-platform sales where FBA inventory is situated in Quebec and taxable turnover exceeds the threshold.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: No real-time fiscal clearance, continuous-transaction-control (CTC) mandate, digital stamping or government API pre-clearance is currently in force in Canada or Quebec. Compliance is achieved through full electronic invoice retention and periodic return filing, not live reporting. Quebec announced (Budget 2023-24) a phased mandatory B2B electronic-invoicing obligation (PEPPOL-compliant) beginning in 2027 for large enterprises; until then paper and PDF invoices remain valid. GST/HST and QST returns must be filed electronically (GST34 and QST return forms via CRA and RQ portals) and each invoice must show the registration number and separate GST and QST amounts to support input tax credits (ITCs) and refund claims; Amazon Marketplace issues its own tax invoices for GST/QST collected on facilitated sales.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Goods physically exported from Canada are zero-rated under ETA Schedule VI, Part V and corresponding QST rules, provided the LP obtains and retains documentary proof of export demonstrating delivery to a destination outside Canada; services supplied to non-residents (offshore services) are zero-rated under ETA Schedule VI, Part V, s. 7 where the recipient is a non-resident and, except for services relating to Canadian real property or tangible personal property situated in Canada, the service qualifies for zero-rating; domestic FBA sales delivered to Canadian consumers are taxable at 14.975% and do not qualify for zero-rating; claims must link each supply to physical removal from Canada and be supportable at the time of the return filing.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Commercial Invoice and Sales Contract with foreign destination and Incoterms demonstrating transfer of risk outside Canada
Carrier and Freight-Forwarder Waybills with Packing Lists
CBSA Export Reporting Record (B13A Export Declaration or approved EDI transmission; small-value courier export reporting exemption retained where applicable)
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: CRA and RQ conduct targeted export-verification audits requiring the documentation bundle to be retained for six years; failure to substantiate zero-rating results in reassessment of GST/QST at 14.975% with arrears interest and penalties under ETA s. 280 (5% plus 1% per month, maximum 17%) and equivalent Quebec administrative penalties; false or grossly negligent export claims attract penalties of up to 50% of the tax evaded under ETA s. 285 and the Quebec Tax Administration Act; criminal liability arises under ETA s. 327 and ITA s. 239 (fines up to 200% of the tax obtained and imprisonment up to five years); the normal four-year reassessment period is extended to ten years where misrepresentation, neglect or fraud is established, permitting retrospective clawback of refunded GST/QST and denied input tax credits.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Bank of Canada (central bank) and Financial Transactions and Reports Analysis Centre of Canada (FINTRAC) as enforcement authority under the Proceeds of Crime (Money Laundering) and Terrorist Financing Act; no centralized exchange-control administration exists—Canada maintains free capital movements under the Currency Act.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: Full convertibility on both current and capital accounts; Canada imposes no exchange-control restrictions or prior approval requirements for profit remittance. Distributions from a Quebec limited partnership to non-resident partners are freely transferable but are subject to Part XIII non-resident withholding tax (25% subject to treaty reduction) and must be reported by the payer via Form NR4. Cross-border remittances exceeding $10,000 CAD are reportable to FINTRAC under the cross-border currency or monetary instruments reporting regime.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: None. Canada does not impose mandatory surrender, repatriation, or conversion ratios for export receipts. Amazon FBA sales proceeds may be retained in foreign-currency accounts or converted at market rates without statutory obligation; however, for income tax purposes all receipts must be translated into Canadian dollars using the Bank of Canada annual average exchange rate in accordance with section 261 of the Income Tax Act.

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Feasibility Rating: Medium-High with legal constraints. Canada does not recognize the 'EMI' licensing category; overseas digital money institutions (e.g., Payoneer, Airwallex, and UK EMI-type entities) may operate as Money Service Businesses registered with FINTRAC and, if offering retail payment accounts in Canadian dollars, must comply with the Retail Payment Activities Act (RPAA) and be registered with the Bank of Canada. Such fintechs are viable as disbursement and FX conversion channels for Amazon FBA settlement, but they are generally not authorized to take deposits under the Bank Act (s.524) and cannot replace a Tier-1 bank operating account for the LP's statutory capital and treasury functions. To mitigate regulatory and counterparty risk, use the fintech rail solely for marketplace settlement and maintain principal liquidity in a bank-regulated account.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: For a Quebec limited partnership with non-resident partners, at least one general partner or authorized signatory must complete a live video-interview or physical in-person identity verification at a Canadian Tier-1 bank. Remote onboarding is available at most banks using video call and digital signing, but if any partner is a non-resident jurisdiction requiring enhanced due diligence, physical presence at a branch or a Canadian consulate may be mandated by internal policy. FINTRAC requires every reporting entity to take reasonable steps to identify beneficial owners holding 25% or more of the partnership, and the general partner must provide a current partnership declaration and proof of legal existence.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Non-resident beneficial ownership structure of the limited partnership with opaque chain or multiple jurisdictions.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Certified copy of the limited partnership agreement registered under the Act respecting the legal publicity of enterprises; Registraire des entreprises (Quebec Enterprise Registrar) current certificate of immatriculation; complete register of beneficial owners; government-issued identification and source-of-wealth documentation for every partner holding 25% or more; and a notarized partnership resolution authorizing account opening.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Limited partnership not yet registered or lacking good standing in Quebec; corporate existence cannot be confirmed.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Quebec Enterprise Registrar immatriculation number, valid attestation of registration, and recent certificate of good standing; if imported from another Canadian jurisdiction, an extra-provincial registration certificate under the Act respecting the legal publicity of enterprises and a copy of the partnership deed.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: High-volume cross-border e-commerce flows with no prior operating history and unexpected beneficiary countries.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Detailed business plan including Amazon FBA seller central statements, platform payout reports, pro-forma cash-flow projections, commercial contracts, customs/sales invoices, and an explanation of the cross-border settlement cycle; must satisfy enhanced due diligence under the Proceeds of Crime (Money Laundering) and Terrorist Financing Act regulations.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Use of offshore digital EMI or foreign financial intermediary in the treasury structure, creating layering risk.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Fully disclosed trust and ownership chart; written agreement with the fintech/EMI showing its FINTRAC/MSB registration; breakdown of purpose for each transaction layer; sanctions and negative news screening results; and confirmation that the LP is not acting as an unlicensed money services business.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Compliant protocol for LP capital contributions by non-resident partners: route via SWIFT MT103 to the LP's Tier-1 Canadian bank operational or escrow account, including the ISO 20022 'Purpose' code for capital contribution (e.g., 'CAPT' or equivalent) and explicit narrative referencing the Quebec enterprise number (NEQ) and the limited partnership agreement. Prior to wiring, obtain applicable Canadian tax advice on the deemed disposition rules for contributed property and ensure the wire origin is from the partner's own bank account. Maintain underlying capital call and subscription records; for any cash receipt exceeding $10,000 CAD, the bank will file a Large Cash Transaction Report with FINTRAC.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Amazon FBA payouts are received through Amazon's electronic settlement system via Canadian clearing in CAD to the Tier-1 account. Trade supplier disbursements are executed via SWIFT MT103 with purpose code 'TRADE' or equivalent, referencing commercial invoices. For larger or documentary export transactions, use commercial letters of credit issued under UCP600 through the Canadian bank, with required documents being bill of lading, commercial invoice, and packing list. All outbound payments must be supported by executed contracts, kept available for CRA and FINTRAC audit, and passed through the bank's sanctions filtering system.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Deliverable CAD/USD FX Forwards (bank-offered, plain vanilla)
Non-Deliverable Forwards (NDFs) only for restricted foreign currencies with a fixed reference rate (not applicable to CAD)

mandatory_on_site_statutory_registers: Register of Members, Register of Directors, Minute Book

corporate_income_tax_regime.statutory_headline_rate: 26.5% combined federal (15%) and Quebec (11.5%) general corporate income tax rate. A Limited Partnership is fiscally transparent; income is allocated to partners and taxed at the partner level, with the combined rate applicable to corporate partners and personal rates applicable to individual partners.
corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: No general tax holiday for Amazon FBA retail. Available incentives: federal Small Business Deduction (9% federal + 3.2% Quebec on first CAD 500,000 of active business income) for a qualifying Canadian-controlled private corporation (CCPC) partner; SR&ED investment tax credits for qualifying R&D; Quebec additional tax holiday for manufacturing or innovation activities only upon qualifying. The LP itself is not eligible for the SBD unless a corporate partner owns a direct interest.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Federal: T5013 Partnership Information Return (including Schedule 691 for non-arm's length transactions); filed electronically through CRA's EFILE/E-File service or My Business Gateway.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: The earlier of (a) the day that is five months after the partnership's fiscal year-end and (b) the earliest day on which any partner is required to file an income tax return. For calendar-year partnerships with individual partners, the T5013 is generally due April 30; for corporate partners with a December year-end, due March 31. If a non-resident partner is subject to Canadian tax, the deadline is also aligned to that partner's return due date.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Business income (or loss) of each partner from the partnership's FBA e-commerce business.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Non-resident partners receiving a Canadian-source allocation must report Box 20 in a Canadian tax return (T1 or T2). The partnership must provide a separate T5013 Statement to each non-resident partner and include a list of non-resident partners with their residency tax identification numbers.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Net investment income other than business income (e.g., interest, dividends, royalties) generated by the partnership.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Canadian-source investment income may be subject to Part XIII withholding. The partnership should withhold the required amount under paragraph 214(1) or rely on treaty relief only after receiving a TRC and proper NR forms from the partner.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Foreign source income and foreign tax credits claimed by the partnership and allocated to partners.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Non-resident partners are generally not entitled to Canadian foreign tax credits for foreign income not connected to Canada; foreign taxes may be claimed in the partner's home jurisdiction. Guidance is required to avoid double taxation.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Failure to file T5013: penalty of CAD 100 per day per partner, up to a maximum of CAD 2,500 for each form, plus interest and late-filing penalties under s. 162(7). Knowingly making false statements carries additional penalties of up to CAD 5,000 or 25% of the understated income, and criminal sanctions for evasion.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Quebec: Relevé 15 (RL-15) Partnership Income; filed electronically via Revenu Québec's Online Services (clicSÉQ and E-Services) and a prescribed provincial election on the partnership annual return (CO-17).
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: The RL-15 must be filed and provided to partners by the same deadline as the federal T5013. For a partnership year ending December 31, due the earlier of April 30 (individual partners) or four months after the partnership year-end if all partners are corporations.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Quebec business income (loss) allocated to the partner before the Quebec additional tax credits.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: A non-resident partner's Quebec allocation is computed under sections 505 et seq. of the Taxation Act. Quebec-source income must be reported on Quebec Form TP-1022 if the partner is non-resident and carries on a business in Quebec. The LP must identify non-resident partners on Schedule 5 of the CO-17 return.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Quebec investment income allocated to the partner, including interest and rental income sourced in Quebec.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Withholding may apply under section 1015 of the Taxation Act for distributions to non-residents. Treaty reduction requires a Canada-Quebec Agreement or Canada-US treaty and submission of Form TP-1059 and a Certificate of Residency.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late filing penalties for Relevé 15 are levied under the Tax Administration Act (QL): CAD 25 per day up to CAD 2,500, plus 10% of unpaid taxes for failure to report income; criminal prosecution possible for falsified statements.

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.statutory_dividend_wht_rate: 25% Part XIII withholding on dividends paid by a Canadian corporation to a non-resident, reduced to 15% under most DTA treaties, and 5% for dividends paid to a treaty-resident corporation holding at least 10% of the voting stock. An LP's profit distribution is not a dividend; for a non-resident partner, the relevant mechanism is Part XIII withholding on guaranteed payments, fees, and certain property distributions, or the non-resident partner's individual/corporate income tax filing on allocated income.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: To obtain reduced withholding, the non-resident must provide an electronic NR301 (for tax treaty benefits) along with a Certificate of Residency (TRC) issued by the tax authority of the residency. For a partnership, the non-resident partner must file Form NR303 for disposition of partnership interests. The payer must retain the forms before releasing payment and remit the reduced rate. In Quebec, Form TP-1059-V is used to claim exemption or reduced withholding under a tax convention.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: Statutory rates on payments to non-residents: royalties = 25%, interest = 25%. Treaty rates with most jurisdictions (e.g., US, UK, Netherlands) reduce interest to 0% (arm's length) and royalties to 10% (copyright royalties 0% or 5% for software). Payments for mixed IP must be split according to character.

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: CAD 1,000,000 aggregate threshold for annual transactions (purchases, sales, interest, royalties, management fees) with non-arm's length non-residents triggers mandatory filing of Form T106 (Specified Transaction Reporting) and preparation of contemporaneous transfer pricing documentation. Master File/Local File are not separately designated under Canadian law, but CRA's IC 87-2R requires comparable OECD-compliant documentation for significant transactions; CbC reporting applies for multinational groups with consolidated revenue of EUR 750 million or more.
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: Canada does not operate an Economic Substance Regulations (ESR) regime as in the UAE. However, CRA applies the General Anti-Avoidance Rule (GAAR, ITA s. 245) to disregard artificial transactions lacking genuine business purpose or commercial substance. For limited partnerships, the partnership must maintain real operational substance (inventory, logistics contracts, bank accounts, arm's length bookkeeping) to sustain limited liability and prevent reallocation of income to a permanent establishment (PE) under Article V of tax treaties.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Deliberate omission of Amazon Marketplace sales revenue, phantom purchases to reduce taxable income, or concealment of the Quebec PE by routing sales through a foreign affiliate without actual logistic or contractual substance.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Criminal prosecution under s. 239(1) ITA and s. 379 of the Tax Administration Act (Quebec): fine of up to 200% of tax evaded; imprisonment of up to 5 years; civil penalty under s. 163(2) ITA of 50% of the understatement plus interest and late penalties.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors and general partners are jointly and severally liable for unpaid source deductions and GST/HST under s. 227.1 ITA; criminal conviction triggers travel bans and extradition, plus personal asset seizure for restitution.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Failure to Withhold Part XIII / Quebec Withholding Tax
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Distributing profits, interest, royalties, management fees, or guaranteed payments to a non-resident partner (e.g., US or Hong Kong-based Amazon vendor) without the mandatory 25% Part XIII withholding or treaty documentation.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Liability as trustee under s. 215 of the ITA for the full withheld amount, plus interest and penalties of 10% each year late; penalty under s. 227(8) ITA can be up to 20% of the unremitted amount.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors and general partners are personally liable for withholding remittances under s. 227.1; failure to settle may lead to civil garnishment, Director's liability certificates, and in aggravated cases, director prosecution for fraudulent concealment.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Charging a non-arm's length foreign affiliate (e.g., Amazon related entity in Delaware/Ireland) an unreasonable markup, cost inflation, or royalty on sales made from the Canadian inventory, while not filing T106 or contemporaneous documentation.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Transfer pricing adjustment under s. 247(2) adding the arm's-length profit to Canadian income; penalty under s. 247(3) of 10% of the net adjustment, minimum CAD 5,000; may be contested only if the taxpayer has made reasonable efforts to use the documented methodology.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors of a corporate general partner can be sued for knowing participation in an adjustment, especially if they signed inaccurate T106 forms. The CRA may use the 'de facto director' doctrine to pierce the LP veil and seek restitution from principals.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Using the Quebec LP as a pure invoicing shell for Amazon FBA sales without maintaining bookkeeping, office assets, inventory control in Canada, or a substantive PE; artificially booking all profit in a no-tax foreign entity while the seller's actual business is managed from Canada.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Reassessment to allocate the entire Canadian-source income to the LP partners; application of GAAR to ignore the scheme; treaty anti-abuse rules may deny the foreign entity's treaty benefits; Quebec's Finances Publiques Act may impose asset freezing and administrative fines.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: The directors/general partners may be deemed personally liable for unpaid tax through the limited partnership's failure to file accurate returns; civil non-payment can lead to Quebec court-ordered travel bans (seizure of passports), and criminal designation as an artificial transaction subject to imprisonment under s. 239 of the Income Tax Act.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Handling Amazon payout funds through unregistered payment processors or cash equivalents without adequate beneficial ownership transparency; failing to register as a money services business (MSB) in Canada if providing payment routing services, or failing to verify high-risk FBA merchants under the Proceeds of Crime (Money Laundering) and Terrorist Financing Act.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: FINTRAC penalties of up to CAD 1,000,000 for a non-compliance record at the LP or general partner level; criminal prosecution for laundering proceeds of a tax fraud, with imprisonment up to 5 years and forfeiture of assets.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: General partners of an LP are personally subject to FINTRAC compliance obligations; a director convicted of AML negligence may be fined up to CAD 250,000 or imprisoned. Quebec civil seizure orders can be issued against director's personal estate.
